title: Console: Slimline Essentials - scope reduction and acceptance criteria for dashboards / tracing / cost breakdown
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Background:
The original Console PRD called for a broad set of observability surfaces (full dashboard cards, long-trace explorer, and route-level + token-level cost breakdown). Engineering capacity and cost constraints require we trim scope to guarantee a stable alpha by the scheduled release. This ticket captures a proposed set of cuts, rationale, acceptance criteria, and rollout notes.

Goals:
- Ship a reliable, low-friction Console alpha that surfaces the most actionable signals for SREs and platform engineers while minimizing engineering and infra cost.
- Preserve the developer experience for model/route troubleshooting and cost triage.
- Enable incremental follow-ups that restore or expand features after alpha.

Proposed scope reductions (Slimline Essentials):
1) Dashboards: provide 3 atomic cards instead of the full 9-card set. Cards kept: Route-throughput (qps + 95p latency), Error-rate timeline, and Cost-by-route (daily). Remove: inference-quality cards, detailed token breakdown cards, and derived anomaly detection for alpha. Cards will be pre-baked and non-customizable.
2) Tracing: ship a lightweight trace list with top-level metadata (trace_id, route, duration, status, start_time) and a 30-second inline preview. Disable full span-level timeline and flamegraph for alpha. Deep trace exploration will open an external temporary viewer (internal tool) rather than a first-party heavy UI.
3) Cost breakdown: surface route-level daily cost and per-1000-token estimate. Do NOT implement per-token breakdown, per-user attribution, or token provenance linking in alpha. Provide CSV export of the route-level cost table for finance teams.
4) Sampling & retention: reduce tracing retention to 7 days for alpha and sample traces at 10% for non-error requests. Errors are retained at 100% for 30 days.
5) Rollouts & guardrails: remove canary toggle UI for now — enable feature via config behind launch only.

Why these cuts:
- Engineering: full span visualization requires substantial front-end and storage work (span normalization, heavy UI perf), which can push release 4+ weeks out.
- Cost: token-level cost tracking multiplies ingestion volume and storage tiering needs. Route-level keeps unit economics visible while controlling ingest.
- UX: shipping fewer, focused cards reduces QA surface and provides clearer immediate value.

Non-goals (explicitly out-of-scope for alpha):
- Custom dashboard builder
- Token-level cost provenance
- Live flamegraphs and span grouping
- Per-tenant RBAC differences for telemetry (alpha uses org-wide view)

Risks:
- Some enterprise customers expect token-level attribution; this will be a known limitation.
- Reduced retention may hinder post-incident forensics beyond 7 days for non-error traces.

Mitigations:
- Document limitations in the alpha release notes and provide a support playbook for customers who need longer retention (manual export procedures).
- Offer an upgrade path in the roadmap that describes restoring token-level cost and extended retention as part of subscription tiers.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Product: Ava Thompson (creator), Priya Sharma (director)
- Eng: Diego Morales (assignee), Eng infra leads (ENG-21034)
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: Three atomic cards render within 2s on initial load and reflect data delays no greater than 5 minutes
Dashboards: UX is non-customizable (no add/remove card actions exposed) and mobile layout is acceptable for basic reading
Tracing: Trace list shows at least 95% of error traces within 10s of ingestion and supports a 30-second inline preview for any selected trace
Tracing: Deep trace links open the documented external viewer and handed-off trace data respects redaction policies
Cost: Route-level daily cost table can be exported to CSV and shows previous 30 days; values match billing system within 2%
Sampling & retention: Non-error traces are sampled at 10% and retained 7 days; error traces retained 30 days
Performance & reliability: Alpha pages maintain 99% successful load rate under a staging traffic profile (50k daily requests simulated)
Docs & support: Release notes and a limitation FAQ are published in Confluence and linked from the alpha Console
Telemetry: Key metrics (card load latency, trace ingestion lag, CSV export success rate) are instrumented and dashboarded for launch monitoring
decisions: Keep route-level cost and drop token-level cost for alpha
Ship a trimmed tracing surface (list + preview) and defer full span explorer
Provide CSV export as a stopgap for finance workflows
tradeoffs: Reduced forensic capability vs. faster time-to-market
Lower storage/cost footprint vs. less granular billing data
Simpler UX vs. lack of customizability for power users
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha internal, week 1): enable feature for internal orgs; monitor telemetry for 72h. Phase 2 (closed beta, week 2-3): invite 3 pilot customers with support on-call; collect feedback and bug reports. Phase 3 (public alpha, week 4): open to all sign-ups with clear limitation messaging. Toggle controlled via backend flag until public alpha completed.
notes: Follow-up tickets to restore features after alpha: PM-restore-token-cost, PM-expand-trace-explorer, ENG-increase-trace-retention. Need legal sign-off on CSV export and PII redaction before public alpha. Schedule a 30-minute pre-launch review with infra and security on 2026-03-25.
